sources.title: Snyk Security Research: Zip Slip vulnerability
sources.version: repo as of retrieval; disclosure 2018-06-05 per page
sources.keyEvidence: Disclosure June 5 2018 by Snyk; affected 'thousands of projects'; vulnerable pattern File(destinationDir, e.getName()) without path validation; example entry name '../../evil.sh'; fix: canonicalize each extracted path and verify it stays inside the destination directory; affected libraries list spans Java/JS/.NET/Ruby/Go/Python/PHP/Perl/Clojure/Rust.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 documentation
sources.version: docs current at retrieval (SQLite docs for FTS5)
sources.keyEvidence: Four built-in tokenizers: unicode61 (default, Unicode 6.1, case-insensitive, token chars L*/N*/Co, remove_diacritics 0/1/2 with documented multi-diacritic bug in mode 1 e.g. U+1ED9), ascii, porter (wrapper), trigram (substring matching + LIKE/GLOB index, min 3 chars, options case_sensitive, remove_diacritics). ICU tokenizer NOT documented in FTS5 page (ICU is a legacy FTS3/4 module); custom tokenizers via C API.

sources.title: SQLite 3.34.0 release log
sources.keyEvidence: 'Enhanced [FTS5] to support [trigram indexes]' in the 3.34.0 changelog (line names trigram indexes; the trigram tokenizer ships in this series).

sources.title: The Update Framework (TUF) specification + homepage
sources.version: spec v1.0.36, revision 2026-08-05, status Living Standard; homepage copyright 2026, CC BY 4.0, CNCF graduated
sources.keyEvidence: Detects/mitigates: arbitrary installation, endless data, extraneous dependencies, fast-forward, indefinite freeze, malicious mirrors, mix-and-match, rollback, key compromise (threshold), wrong software installation. Roles: root (trust anchor, key rotation), targets (hashes/sizes, delegation), snapshot (consistent target-metadata versions), timestamp (online, short-freshness, limits stale replay).

sources.title: Uptane (uptane.org)
sources.version: homepage as of retrieval; Linux Foundation JDF project
sources.keyEvidence: 'A Secure Software Update Framework for Automobiles'; 'Acknowledging that all systems will eventually be hacked, Uptane is designed to minimize the damage of a compromise and assure rapid recovery'; layered degradation. Director/Image split and partial-verification details live in the Standard (not fetched this arm — uncertainty noted).

sources.title: Chromium OS update_engine README (A/B updates)
sources.keyEvidence: Update written to inactive partition while system runs from active; partition re-read, hashed, compared to metadata hash; postinstall writes dm-verity tree; updater 'periodically checkpoints the last operation ... can continue from the point it missed' after failure/shutdown; failed update: 'The user will continue on the old version'; failed boot: 'rollback to the old partition'; delta payload with fallback to full after repeated failures.

sources.title: Android A/B (seamless) system updates
sources.version: Android docs current at retrieval; Virtual A/B since Android 10
sources.keyEvidence: Two slots; unused slot receives OTA while device runs; 'This approach makes updates fault resistant by keeping the unused slot as a fallback'; interrupted updates resumable; failed boot 'reboot back into the old partition and remains usable'; 'Virtual A/B updates have replaced Legacy A/B system updates in Android 10'.

sources.title: OSTree (libostree) documentation
sources.keyEvidence: 'checksums individual files and has a content-addressed-object store'; 'checks out the files via hardlinks, and they thus need to be immutable'; 'Transactional upgrades and rollback for the system'; multiple parallel bootable deployments; bootloader configuration managed by libostree. (Per-deployment symlink/boot-swap details are in Deployments docs, not fetched this arm — noted.)

sources.title: DOMPurify (Cure53)
sources.version: v3.4.16 shown on README at retrieval; project since 2014-02; Apache-2.0/MPL-2.0
sources.keyEvidence: 'DOM-only, super-fast, uber-tolerant XSS sanitizer for HTML, MathML and SVG'; 'works with a secure default'; post-sanitization DOM modification 'can easily void the effects of sanitization'; jsdom required current on server; happy-dom 'not considered safe at this point'; CI across 9 browser/OS combos + fuzzing of sanitize() and CONFIG.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation)
sources.version: W3C Recommendation, published 2024-12-12; supersedes/extends 2.1 (2018-06); 4.1.1 Parsing removed
sources.keyEvidence: Kiosk-relevant SCs: 1.4.3 contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large); 1.4.11 non-text contrast 3:1; 1.4.12 text spacing; 2.4.7 focus visible; 2.5.1 single-pointer alternative for path/multipoint gestures; 2.5.5 target size 44x44 (AAA); 2.5.7 dragging alternative (AA, new in 2.2); 2.5.8 target size min 24x24 (AA, new in 2.2); 1.3.4 orientation (fixed-orientation kiosks need essential justification).
